Does `serve_owner_request` take `ByteStream` as a separate contract parameter, or does it take only `HttpRequest` whose body is a `ByteStream`; in the latter case, does its runtime code directly name `ByteStream` or receive it only transitively through `HttpRequest`?

quotes:
`models`, for `HttpRequest`, `ByteStream` and `HttpResponse`, which its
surface takes and answers, `OwnerRequest`, `OwnerValues`, `OwnerAdmission`
and `OwnerAction`, which it reads, builds and matches, and `OperationAnswer`
with every variant of it and `RefusalCode`, which it renders;
judgement.why: Whether `ByteStream` is a separate parameter, a field type or another directly named contract symbol is a State 6 signature and schema question.

topics.topic: Whether data_provider ownership of OWNER_ACTIONS conflicts with owner_interface ownership of route selection
questions: Does owning `OWNER_ACTIONS`, whose method-and-path rows determine which action a request names, violate the prohibition on owning selection, or does `data_provider` own only the route facts while `owner_interface` owns the selection algorithm?

quotes: Any check the server makes: the forms carry values, `operations` decides.
judgement.why: P10 already judged the same ownership question on the unchanged passages: `data_provider` owns the inert route rows, while consumers own their use and `operations` owns checks.

precedent.topic: Module responsible for OWNER_ACTIONS routing and behavioral classifications
quotes: Any check the server makes: the forms carry values, `operations` decides.
precedent.why: The table and its inert release values belong to `data_provider`, while `owner_interface` consumes them and `operations` owns the resulting checks and decisions.

topics.topic: Whether upload-body failure handling includes stream failures occurring after a valid multipart head
questions: Does “a body ... that fails” include a file-part stream that fails after a valid head, or only failures encountered before the unread file stream is handed on?

quotes:
A stream that ends before the closing delimiter is a failure
of the file part's stream, which `migration_import` refuses as a file that
cannot be read (`file_unreadable`), replacing nothing kept (A16 rule 2).
judgement.why: P9 already judged this exact post-head stream-failure question on the unchanged passage.

precedent.topic: Handling failure of an upload file stream after a valid head
quotes:
A stream that ends before the closing delimiter is a failure
of the file part's stream, which `migration_import` refuses as a file that
cannot be read (`file_unreadable`), replacing nothing kept (A16 rule 2).
precedent.why: The text expressly assigns failure after a valid head has been handed on to the file-part stream and requires `migration_import` to return `file_unreadable`.

topics.topic: Which module reads the underlying ByteStream while migration_import consumes the UploadBody port
questions: Who performs reads on the underlying request `ByteStream`: does `upload_framing` perform them while `migration_import` drives the `UploadBody` port, or must `migration_import` read framing bytes itself despite multipart syntax being hidden?

quotes:
Reading the body's head alone
— the boundary the request's content type names, the first part, which
must be the CSRF field, the form field the data provider's
`OWNER_CSRF_FIELD` names (owner, 2026-11-24), and the second part's headers — at most the
data provider's `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES`, answering the CSRF value, or
none for a head of another form or longer than the bound; and the file
part's bytes as a stream that ends where the part ends, read only when its
reader asks and never buffered beyond the delimiter it must look ahead for;

Any check of the CSRF value (`owner_sessions`), the size limit of the file
and its reading (`migration_import`, A19 rule 4), the HTTP server and its
connection (`instance_lifecycle`), the forms and pages (`owner_interface`).
judgement.why: `upload_framing` owns the delimiter-aware stream that reads the underlying body on demand, while `migration_import` drives that stream and owns file consumption and the size limit.

topics.topic: Which validations and decisions are included in owner_interface's responsibility for checks
questions: Does “any check” include HTTP readability, multipart-head validity, form decoding and route matching, which `owner_interface` is also required to detect, or only authentication, authorization, value, revision and lifecycle decisions?

quotes:
A
request it cannot read — a body or a head that fails, a form that cannot be
decoded — is handed on with no values, nothing partly read kept, and
answered by `operations` as any other; it never closes the connection
instead of answering (owner, 2026-11-24, option (a) of the question State 4
carried to State 7).
Any check the server makes: the forms carry values, `operations` decides.
judgement.why: `owner_interface` detects and represents syntactic reading or decoding failure by handing on no values, but `operations` owns the resulting admission and operation decision.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
